classification.difficultyReason: Factor a quadratic first derivative, evaluate an exact fractional ordinate and classify two stationary points using the second derivative.

content.prompt: Find and classify the stationary points on $f(x)=x^3-4x^2+4x$.

spec.description: Cubic through the origin, with a local maximum in the first quadrant and a local minimum touching the positive x-axis. Both axes and curve ends have arrowheads; no ticks or numerical labels.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied curve and axes only; no stationary-point coordinates or classifications.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f'(x)&=3x^2-8x+4\\(3x-2)(x-2)&=0\\x&=\frac23,\ 2\\f\!\left(\frac23\right)&=\frac8{27}-\frac{16}{9}+\frac83\\&=\frac{32}{27}\\f(2)&=8-16+8\\&=0\\f''(x)&=6x-8\\f''\!\left(\frac23\right)&=4-8\\&=-4<0\\f''(2)&=12-8\\&=4>0\end{align*}$$
Hence there is a maximum at $\left(\frac23,\frac{32}{27}\right)$ and a minimum at $(2,0)$.
